title: Rules
text: Rules report problems in a BibTeX project. Run biblint rule to list them, or biblint rule <name> for one rule’s summary.

title: Rules
text:
Rule reference









Rule
Default
Fix
Purpose




syntax_error
yes
none
BibTeX syntax is incomplete or unbalanced.


formatting
no
safe/configured
The file would be reformatted by biblint.


missing_key
yes
none
An entry has no citation key.


key_format
no
none
An existing key differs from the configured key formula.


duplicate_key
yes
none
A citation key is used more than once.


duplicate_doi
no
none
Two entries share a DOI.


duplicate_citation
no
none
Two entries share a normalized citation fingerprint.


duplicate_abstract
no
none
Two entries share an abstract fingerprint.


duplicate_field
yes
none
An entry repeats a field name.


empty_field
yes
none
A field has no value.


nonstandard_name_separator
yes
none
A name-list field uses with or a comma before and.


invalid_suppression
yes
none
A suppression comment is malformed, misplaced, or obsolete.


unsupported_escape
yes
none
A character has no built-in LaTeX escape.


unsupported_construct
yes
none
Source was preserved because it could not be structured.



syntax_error has error severity. Most other structural problems are warnings; preserved source and unsupported characters are notes.
nonstandard_name_separator checks author, editor, translator, and collaborator values. It only examines text outside nested braces, does not rewrite values, and does not inspect prose fields such as title or note.

title: Rules
text:
Inline suppressions
A standalone % biblint-ignore <rule> [<rule> ...][: <reason>] comment suppresses the named rules for the next BibTeX entry:
% biblint-ignore nonstandard_name_separator duplicate_field
@book{garfinkel1997,
  author = {Simson Garfinkel with Gene Spafford},
}
The reason after : is optional. Multiple comments before one entry are also combined. Suppressions cannot hide syntax errors or whole-file formatting diagnostics. Malformed, misplaced, or unused directives are reported by invalid_suppression.
Formatting is not enabled for check by default because it is a mechanical rewrite rather than a content diagnostic. Use check --format to include it, select formatting in biblint.toml, or use format --check as a formatting-only gate.

title: Rules
text:
Selecting rules
[lint]
select = ["duplicate_key"]
extend-select = ["key_format", "duplicate_doi"]
ignore = ["unsupported_escape"]
select replaces the default set. extend-select adds rules, and ignore takes precedence. Use all as a wildcard. Per-file exceptions use the same rule names:
[lint.per-file-ignores]
"generated/**" = ["formatting", "unsupported_construct"]

title: Rules
text:
Project-level checks
When checking a directory or multiple files, biblint also detects duplicates across files. DOI, citation, and abstract rules are disabled by default; enable only the comparisons useful for the project.

title: Rules
text:
Key-format checks
key_format is disabled by default because changing a citation key can break references elsewhere. Enable it explicitly:
[lint]
extend-select = ["key_format"]

[lint.key-format]
style = "better-bibtex"
The rule reports a suggestion but does not rename keys automatically. See Citekey generation to configure the formula.

title: biblint
text: biblint is a BibTeX linter and formatter. Commit biblint.toml so collaborators and CI use the same policy.

title: biblint
text:
Commands
biblint check .
biblint check . --format
biblint check references.bib --format --fix
biblint check references.bib --format --fix --unsafe-fixes
biblint check . --output json
biblint format references.bib
biblint format . --check
biblint format references.bib --diff
biblint rule
biblint rule duplicate_key
check reports syntax and lint diagnostics by default. check --format additionally reports whether files would be reformatted. format writes the configured representation, --check reports whether a file would change, and --diff prints the change without writing it.
Both commands accept files, directories, and standard input (-). Directories contribute .bib files recursively. See Configuration for discovery and policy settings.

title: biblint
text:
Workflow
Use check to review a project and format to apply its configured format:
biblint check .
biblint check . --format --fix
biblint format references.bib --diff
check --format --fix applies safe formatting changes. Key generation, merging, field removal, brace removal, and author truncation also require --unsafe-fixes.

title: biblint
text:
Defaults
Without a configuration file, format normalizes layout, entry types, and field names while preserving value spelling. Other transforms and optional checks are enabled in biblint.toml.

text:

title: Development
text:
biblint is a Rust 2024 workspace with four crates:
The minimum supported Rust version is 1.88. Keep parser, formatter, and rule changes lossless: source biblint cannot structure must remain visible rather than being dropped.

title: Development
text:
Checks
Run the workspace checks before submitting changes:
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace

title: Development
text:
Adding behavior
Keep formatting policy in biblint-format, configuration and diagnostics in biblint-core, and CLI concerns in biblint. Add focused regression tests for new transforms and rules.
The citekey formula evaluator follows the same rule: its syntax is inspired by Better BibTeX, but its implementation and tests live in biblint and operate on BibTeX data only. Do not add a Zotero-only construct unless there is a deterministic BibTeX representation for its inputs.

title: Development
text:
Rendering the docs
The documentation source is in docs/ and is rendered as a Quarto website:
quarto render docs

title: Configuration
text: biblint.toml contains formatting policy, rule selection, and file discovery. The command line chooses the operation and output format.

title: Configuration
text:
Discovery
Without --config, biblint searches upward from the input path. An explicitly supplied config path takes precedence. Commit one config file at the repository root so collaborators and CI share the policy.
The top-level file-selection settings apply to both check and format:
include = ["**/*.bib"]
exclude = ["vendor/**"]
default-exclude = true
Directories contribute .bib files recursively. Explicit file arguments are accepted regardless of extension. With default-exclude = true, .git/** and target/** are skipped.

title: Configuration
text:
Rule selection
[lint]
# `select` replaces the default rule set.
select = ["duplicate_key", "duplicate_doi"]

# `extend-select` adds rules without removing defaults.
extend-select = ["key_format"]

# `ignore` wins over selection.
ignore = ["unsupported_escape"]

[lint.per-file-ignores]
"generated/**" = ["formatting"]
Use all as a wildcard. If select is omitted, default-enabled rules run. extend-select adds opt-in rules, while ignore takes precedence. Per-file ignores use the same rule names.
The formatting rule is opt-in for check. Use biblint check --format for a one-off check or add it to select/extend-select in the configuration. biblint format --check checks formatting independently of lint rule selection.

title: Configuration
text:
Starter configuration
include = ["**/*.bib"]
exclude = ["vendor/**", "generated/**"]
default-exclude = true

[lint]
extend-select = ["duplicate_doi", "duplicate_citation", "key_format"]

[lint.key-format]
style = "better-bibtex"

[format]
indent = 2
align = false
lowercase = true
sort = ["key"]
sort-fields = ["title", "author", "year"]

[format.key-generation]
formula = "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1,0)"
The formula is optional because it is biblint’s default. See Citekey generation for the available syntax.

title: Configuration
text:
Validation
Unknown settings, rule names, invalid globs, and invalid formulas are rejected when the configuration is loaded. Settings not specified in the file use their defaults.

title: Formatting
text: biblint format writes a canonical representation of the BibTeX it understands. By default it changes layout, entry-type spelling, and field-name spelling only.

title: Formatting
text:
Default shape
Input:
@ARTICLE{Smith2024,
author={Smith, John},
title={A Study},
year=2024
}
Default output:
@article{Smith2024,
  author = {Smith, John},
  title = {A Study},
  year = 2024
}
The default does not align equals signs, sort entries or fields, add braces, change values, or remove duplicate and empty fields. It separates entries with a blank line.

title: Formatting
text:
Layout and ordering
[format]
indent = 2                 # a space count, or "tab"
align = false              # or a field-name column number
blank-lines = true
trailing-commas = true
wrap = 80                  # false disables wrapping
sort = ["key"]
sort-fields = ["title", "author", "year"]
align = false disables alignment. sort = true uses key order, and sort-fields = true uses biblint’s built-in field order. Lists provide an explicit order.

title: Formatting
text:
Value transforms
These settings are opt-in because they alter value spelling or representation:







Setting
Effect




curly
Enclose values in braces.


numeric
Render numeric values as bare literals.


months
Normalize recognized month names.


format-page-ranges
Normalize page ranges.


escape / unescape
Convert supported text between Unicode and LaTeX.


encode-urls
Encode URL underscores.


strip-enclosing-braces
Remove one outer brace group.


enclosing-braces / remove-braces
Select fields whose brace depth changes.


drop-all-caps
Convert all-caps values to title case.


wrap
Wrap long values at a configured width.


lowercase
Lowercase entry types and field names. Enabled by default.



The escape table is package-independent. Unconvertible characters are preserved and reported by unsupported_escape.

title: Formatting
text:
Cleanup and semantic transforms
[format]
remove-empty-fields = true
remove-duplicate-fields = true
omit = ["abstract"]
strip-comments = true
tidy-comments = true
max-authors = 3
generate-keys = true
duplicate-kinds = ["doi", "citation"]
merge = "combine"
These settings can remove information, change author lists, generate keys, or merge entries. merge accepts first, last, combine, and overwrite. By default it considers DOI, citation, and abstract duplicates. Add key to duplicate-kinds to include key duplicates.
generate-keys uses the same formula evaluator as the key_format rule. See Citekey generation for a Better BibTeX syntax subset.

title: Formatting
text:
Fix safety
check --format --fix applies safe formatting edits when formatting is explicitly enabled. For a formatting-only policy check, use biblint format references.bib --check. Transforms that can change content or identity require:
biblint check references.bib --format --fix --unsafe-fixes
The standalone format command applies the configured profile directly.

title: Formatting
text:
Preserved source
Comments, special entries, and unstructured source are retained unless a configured transform targets them. Unstructured source is reported as unsupported_construct rather than discarded.

title: Citekey generation
text:
biblint can check existing citation keys and generate deterministic suggestions from BibTeX entries. The better-bibtex style uses a deterministic subset of Better BibTeX’s formula syntax and reads only data in the .bib file.
Unsupported functions and filters are rejected when the configuration is loaded.


The built-in formula is:
auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1,0)
It:

uses the first creator surname, falling back through author, editor, translator, and collaborator
lowercases that surname
appends the first four digits found in year
appends the first significant word of title

shorttitle removes common stopwords before counting words. The 0 preserves the title fragment’s original capitalization.
For example:
@article{old,
  author = {Smith, John},
  title = {A Study of Things},
  year = {2024}
}
produces the suggestion smith2024Study. By default, collisions receive alphabetic suffixes such as a, b, and aa. Entries without enough key material are left unchanged.



Keep the formula in the repository’s biblint.toml:
[lint]
extend-select = ["key_format"]

[lint.key-format]
style = "better-bibtex"

[format]
generate-keys = true

[format.key-generation]
formula = "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1,0)"
collision-suffix = "alphabetic"
The formula is optional because the example is the default. key_format reports differences but does not rename existing keys. generate-keys = true enables replacement as a formatter transform. With check --format --fix, it requires --unsafe-fixes:
biblint check references.bib --format --fix --unsafe-fixes
biblint format references.bib
For author/year keys that reserve the first suffix letter, use collision-suffix = "skip-a". The following formula uses the full surname for one creator and the first three letters of up to three creators otherwise:
[format.key-generation]
formula = "auth(0,m=2) ? auth(3,m=1) + auth(3,m=2) + auth(3,m=3) + shortyear : auth + shortyear"
collision-suffix = "skip-a"
Creator lists follow standard BibTeX name syntax: separate creators with the word and.



Formula names are case-insensitive. The evaluator supports:

direct BibTeX fields, such as title, doi, and shortauthor
quoted strings and numbers, for example "-" and 2024
concatenation with +
fallbacks with ||, and top-level alternate patterns separated by ; or |
conditional composition with &&
ternaries such as language == "en" ? "eng" : ""
length comparisons using ==, !=, <, <=, >, or >=
chained filters such as auth.lower.clean
positional and named function arguments, such as substring(start=1,n=3)

The implemented entry functions are:

creators: auth, authAuthEa, authEtAl, authEtal2, authForeIni, authIni, authorIni, authorLast, authors, authorsAlpha, authorsn, and authshort
entry fields and metadata: date, extra, firstpage, journal, language, lastpage, month, origdate, origyear, shortyear, title, type, and year
title fragments: shorttitle and veryshorttitle

The implemented filters are abbr, alphanum, ascii, capitalize, clean, condense, default, discard, len, lower, nopunct, nopunctordash, numeric, postfix, prefix, replace, select, skipwords, substring, transliterate, and upper.
For example, this formula uses a short author field from Better BibTeX’s extra data when it is present and otherwise falls back to the BibTeX author:
extra('tex.shortauthor').clean.lower || auth.lower
extra(...) reads matching key: value lines from the BibTeX extra field. Functions and filters outside the supported lists are configuration errors.



The same BibTeX input and committed configuration produce the same suggestions. Existing keys are reserved, and collision suffixes are assigned in document order.
